## Mitigation Checklist

A practical framework for defending against common security risks:

### 1. Principle of Least Privilege
Grant write scope only to the paths a process genuinely needs. Apply this principle at every boundary—system accounts, application processes, and user roles should have no more authority than necessary to perform their legitimate function. Restrict by default, grant only what is required, and review grants regularly.

### 2. Input Validation at Trust Boundaries
Treat all external content as untrusted data, never as instructions. Validate all inputs at system trust boundaries before use. This includes data from external sources, user input, configuration files, and any content arriving across a network or process boundary. Verify type, format, length, and content against a strict allowlist.

### 3. Path Canonicalization
Resolve and validate file paths before any write to block directory traversal attacks. Canonicalize paths to their absolute, resolved form; reject any path that tries to escape the intended directory. Use only the resolved path for access decisions.

### 4. Audit Logging
Record every denied action with its reason for later review. Log all security-relevant events—permission denials, validation failures, policy violations, and anomalies. Include context: what was attempted, why it was denied, by whom, and when. Retain logs for investigation and compliance.
